title: Large-load data-universe completion manifest
purpose: Machine-readable accounting of the public universe searched for Track 3 large-load verification, separating row-level queue data, project-level extractions, aggregate utility/regulator evidence, and genuine publication limits.

markets.scope: PublicQueueReport covers active, complete and withdrawn generator interconnection requests for Cluster 14 and prior; Cluster 15 is a separate official workbook. Project-level large-load requests are not published by CAISO as a per-request queue.
markets.notes: Historical cluster-count/capacity series added separately. Full binary workbook replacement was not performed through the current tool surface because direct XLSX retrieval returned unsupported content type; no rows were fabricated.

markets.scope: Current public endpoint exposes 83 additional >=100 MW requests in the captured dataset but the required state/location fields are absent from the public response used by this registry.
markets.notes: The 83 are held outside row-level core and included only in expanded-known accounting. MISO also states detailed project information is constrained until a GIA is filed with FERC.

markets.scope: PJM publicly exposes serial and cycle service-request tables for generation, merchant transmission and long-term firm transmission service. The public generation tables are not a large-load queue; a separate public per-load-request dataset was not established.
markets.notes: Historical/current service-request evolution is documented; large-load aggregate transparency remains subject to the FERC proceeding and PJM publication process.

markets.scope: ERCOT Batch Zero applies to eligible >=75 MW large loads; September 2026 verification RFIs were issued to a majority of conditionally included ILLEs. ERCOT's public process page publishes forms and guidance, but completed RFI responses are not an open per-project dataset.
markets.notes: No individual Batch Zero rows are invented. Monthly GIS remains the public generator-side interconnection dataset, distinct from large-load intake.

markets.scope: SPP publishes a detailed active generator-interconnection listing and a dedicated HILL framework for large loads, including data centers. The public HILL page provides process/study architecture rather than a per-load customer table.
markets.notes: The load/customer layer is preserved as process and filing evidence; SPP MDAG materials confirm the HILL/HILLGA processes are operating under FERC-approved Docket ER26-247, but the public HILL page does not enumerate a complete customer-level load table.

markets.scope: NYISO publishes a dedicated Load Projects tab in its public interconnection queue. Independent current-readable mirrors expose queue ID, developer, project, MW, county and POI; 12 named load projects are now linked into the project-level extraction layer.
markets.notes: The accessible public universe remains larger than the 12 individually mapped records in this first crosswalk; the source population and accounting are retained rather than claiming a complete facility match.

markets.scope: ISO-NE's public 2026 large-load forecast names a 200 MW data-center project in NEMA and an additional large electrification project, but does not provide the per-project maturity/status ladder needed for a full study-stage history.
markets.notes: Public forecast/project identity evidence is preserved; no study stage is inferred from forecast inclusion.

markets.scope: All 28 Data Load rows from the retained September 2026 queue extraction now have project IDs, names, requested/contract-capacity values and public planning-area/town identities in the project layer.
markets.notes: The public row still does not identify the commercial customer/proponent for these 28 projects. That field remains explicitly unknown rather than inferred.

markets.scope: IESO application status publishes a large connection universe with applicant, name, zone, type, size, target date and status. Six current load/increase-load records are now in the project layer.
markets.notes: Technical feasibility reports may be confidential; OEB CCIM is preserved as a distribution-capacity context layer rather than a fabricated customer list.

markets.scope: Utility, regulator and permit sources beyond the nine organized markets are preserved as discrete projects where public identity is exposed, plus non-additive aggregate demand/service evidence.
markets.notes: Project-level layer now includes 33 Virginia DEQ permits, 35 BPA large-load request records, 28 AESO data-load projects, 12 NYISO load projects, six IESO load applications, eight AEP named projects, two EEI projects, and three named utility-service/contract/distribution records.
